questions.prompt: Which code organization processes every day and resolves all waiting days it can?

choices.label: Resolve all possible pending days before remembering today.
choices.feedback: One warmer day can resolve several pending days. Recording each resolved day before remembering today preserves the pending stack; returning after the scan includes every day.
choices.code:
prepare zero waits and an empty stack of day indices
for each day, from left to right:
  while today resolves the last pending day:
    remove that pending day
    record its waiting distance
  add today's index to the pending days
return all waits after the scan
choices.feedbackCode:
prepare zero waits and an empty stack of day indices
for each day, from left to right:
  while today resolves the last pending day:
    remove that pending day
    record its waiting distance
  add today's index to the pending days
return all waits after the scan

choices.label: Resolve at most one pending day per new day.
choices.feedback: One warmer day can resolve several earlier days. With [73,72,74], resolving only one leaves the first day unresolved: [0,1,0] instead of [2,1,0].
choices.code:
prepare zero waits and an empty stack of day indices
for each day, from left to right:
  if today resolves the last pending day:
    remove that pending day
    record its waiting distance
  add today's index to the pending days
return all waits after the scan

choices.label: Return the waits after processing the first day.
choices.feedback: Returning inside the day loop stops before later temperatures can resolve earlier days. With [73,74], this returns [0,0] instead of [1,0].
choices.code:
prepare zero waits and an empty stack of day indices
for each day, from left to right:
  while today resolves the last pending day:
    remove that pending day
    record its waiting distance
  add today's index to the pending days
  return all waits now

choices.label: Remember today before trying to resolve pending days.
choices.feedback: Today becomes the last pending day and is not warmer than itself, so it blocks earlier days from being resolved. With [73,74], this leaves [0,0] instead of [1,0].
choices.code:
prepare zero waits and an empty stack of day indices
for each day, from left to right:
  add today's index to the pending days
  while today resolves the last pending day:
    remove that pending day
    record its waiting distance
return all waits after the scan
